questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: A patient has sustained high fever of 39 to 40 degrees Celsius, weakness, stomach pain, constipation and headache, and typhoid is suspected. Which test is used to confirm the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Typhoid, caused by Salmonella typhi, is confirmed by the Widal test, which detects the patient's antibodies against the bacterium. ELISA is the test used to detect HIV infection and is the nearest wrong choice, but it is not the confirmatory test for typhoid. Biopsy is used to examine tissue for cancer, and PCR for early detection of HIV or of cancer genes.

questions.stem: On exposure to pollen, a person develops sneezing and watery eyes. Which pair correctly names the type of antibody involved and the cells that release histamine?
questions.explanation: In allergy the immune system overreacts to an allergen such as pollen and makes IgE antibodies, which trigger mast cells to release histamine and serotonin; these cause sneezing and watery eyes. questions.subject: biology
questions.stem:
Arrange the following events of HIV replication in a human host in the correct sequence.
(A) Progeny viruses released into the blood attack other helper T lymphocytes
(B) Viral RNA is copied into DNA by reverse transcriptase
(C) Viral DNA is incorporated into the DNA of the infected cell
(D) HIV enters a macrophage
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: After HIV enters a macrophage, its RNA genome is copied into DNA by reverse transcriptase, and this viral DNA is incorporated into the host cell's DNA, which then directs the production of new viruses. The progeny viruses released into the blood go on to attack helper T lymphocytes. Integration cannot come before reverse transcription, because the viral genome stays RNA until it has been copied.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 Human Health and Disease: AIDS, replication of HIV in macrophages and helper T lymphocytes

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: The behaviour of the cells from the swelling when they are crowded together indicates that they have lost:
questions.explanation: Normal cells stop dividing when they touch their neighbours, a property called contact inhibition, and cancer cells have lost it, so they keep dividing even when crowded and form a lump. Metastasis is the spread of tumour cells to other sites, a property that malignant cells gain rather than lose, so it does not describe this behaviour.
questions.passage_text: A 52-year-old man who has chewed tobacco for thirty years visits a clinic with a hard, painless swelling on the inner lining of his cheek that has not healed for three months. A small piece of the swelling is removed and examined under a microscope. The pathologist reports that the cells from the swelling keep on dividing even when they are crowded against one another, whereas cells from the healthy lining of the same cheek stop dividing once they touch their neighbours. Cells from the swelling are also found in a lymph node of the neck. A genetic test shows that a normal gene which regulates cell division in the cheek cells has been changed so that it stays permanently switched on. The doctor explains that substances present in chewed tobacco can bring about such a change. The surgeon plans to remove the swelling, and the radiation specialist plans to treat the area with a lethal dose of radiation after the operation. The oncologist advises a course of chemotherapy as well. The patient is told that all these steps are meant to remove or destroy the abnormal cells and that regular check-ups will be needed for several years after the treatment.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 Human Health and Disease: cancer, contact inhibition and transformation of normal cells

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: The finding in the lymph node of the neck indicates that the tumour is:

options.text: Benign, because benign tumours remain confined to the site where they arise
Benign, because a hard painless swelling does not harm other tissues
Malignant, because its cells have spread to another part of the body
Malignant, because the swelling has not healed for three months

questions.explanation: Benign tumours stay confined to their site of origin, whereas malignant tumours shed cells that reach other parts of the body, a process called metastasis. questions.stem: The gene change found by the genetic test and the agent that caused it are best described, respectively, as:

options.text: A viral oncogene inserted into host DNA; a chemical carcinogen
A proto-oncogene activated into an oncogene; a chemical carcinogen
A proto-oncogene activated into an oncogene; a physical carcinogen
A viral oncogene inserted into host DNA; a biological carcinogen

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Why is chemotherapy advised for this patient in addition to surgery and radiation?

options.text: The drugs stimulate the immune system to clear the swelling, so no other treatment is needed
The drugs repair the changed gene in the tumour cells and make them normal again
The drugs convert the swelling into a benign tumour so that it need not be removed
The drugs travel through the body and can destroy tumour cells that have spread elsewhere

questions.explanation: Surgery and radiation treat the site of the tumour only, but cells found in a lymph node may already have spread. Which of the following statements about this patient's diagnosis and treatment are correct?
(A) The tobacco substances that changed his gene are chemical carcinogens.
(B) The radiation is directed at the tumour cells, taking care not to damage the neighbouring normal cells.
(C) The chemotherapeutic drugs will destroy only the tumour cells and leave all normal body cells unharmed.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem:
Arrange the following events in the conversion of milk into curd in the correct sequence.
(A) Coagulation and partial digestion of milk proteins by the acid
(B) Addition of a small amount of curd to fresh milk
(C) Multiplication of lactic acid bacteria at a suitable temperature
(D) Production of lactic acid from the sugar of the milk
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: The curd added to fresh milk supplies lactic acid bacteria as a starter. At a suitable temperature they multiply and make lactic acid from the milk sugar, and this acid then coagulates and partially digests the milk proteins to give curd. The acid cannot be formed before the bacteria have been added and have multiplied, so the protein change comes last.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem:
Arrange the following events of the secondary treatment of sewage in the correct sequence.
(A) Aerobic microbes grow into flocs while the BOD of the effluent falls
(B) Effluent from the primary settling tank is aerated in a large tank
(C) The remaining sludge is digested by anaerobic bacteria in digesters
(D) Flocs settle in a settling tank to form activated sludge
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: In secondary treatment the primary effluent is aerated, aerobic microbes grow into flocs and lower the BOD, the flocs settle as activated sludge, and the part of the sludge not returned to the aeration tank goes to anaerobic digesters. Settling cannot come before floc formation, and sludge can be digested only after it has been collected.

Which of the following statements about microbial products are correct?

Suppress the immune response that causes rejection of a transplanted organ

questions.stem: A farmer wants to protect crop roots from fungal pathogens without using chemical fungicides. Which of the following biocontrol agents should the farmer use?

questions.stem: Which photosynthetic, nitrogen-fixing organism is an important biofertiliser in paddy fields and also adds organic matter to the soil?

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem:
Arrange the following steps of the polymerase chain reaction in the correct sequence.
(A) Extension of the primers by Taq polymerase
(B) Annealing of primers to the template strands
(C) Mixing the template DNA, primers, Taq polymerase and nucleotides in a tube
(D) Denaturation of the template DNA by heating
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: A PCR starts with the template, primers, thermostable Taq polymerase and nucleotides in one tube. Heating denatures the double-stranded template, cooling lets the primers anneal to the separated strands, and Taq polymerase then extends the primers. Annealing cannot come before denaturation, because primers can bind only to single strands.
